newsitem.title: USA: Nucor warns Q1, Q2 estimates too high.
newsitem.headline: Nucor warns Q1, Q2 estimates too high.

text.p: John Correnti, president of Nucor Corp, on Tuesday said the consensus first-quarter earnings estimate of $0.81 per share was "probably too rich" because of start-up costs at the company's Berkeley, South Carolina, mill.
"I think that's probably too rich," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Correnti also said Wall Street's consensus second-quarter estimate of $0.90 per share was too high.
Correnti said start-up costs at the Berkely mill and some inventory adjustment costs would hold back second-quarter earnings.
The first-quarter consensus was based on 11 estimates ranging from $0.70 to $1.19, according to First Call. The second-quarter consensus was based on seven estimates ranging from $0.83 to $1.00.
Nucor, a steel producer, posted earnings of $0.60 a share in the previous first quarter and $0.63 in the second quarter.

Commenting on his earnings projections for the four quarters of this year, Correnti said, "I've said this publicly before...$0.70 (for the first quarter), $0.80 (for the second quarter), $0.90 (for the third quarter) and $1.00 (for the fourth quarter.)
"The consensus for the year is $3.33 per share. We're comfortable with that. That's OK for the year," he said.
